predecessors.name: Former Qin
predecessors.text: the land Yao Chang held after leaving Former Qin; the pages give no extent

successors.name: Jin dynasty (Western and Eastern Jin)
successors.text: Jin forces entered Guanzhong and Luoyang in 416-417

ledger.x: 384: Yao Chang rebels against Former Qin and takes the title Everlasting King of Qin.
386: Yao Chang occupies Chang'an and proclaims himself emperor.
386: Chang'an becomes the Later Qin capital.
386: Later Qin and Fu Deng's Former Qin face each other.
394: the Former Qin is destroyed.
394: the Former Qin ends at Feiqiao.
399: Later Qin takes Luoyang from Eastern Jin.
400: Later Qin conquers Western Qin.
401: Later Liang submits after the siege of Guzang.
403: Lü Long surrenders the whole territory.
403: Later Qin annexes the Later Liang.
405: Chouchi submits to Later Qin.
407: Southern Yan and Western Shu submit.
409: Qifu Gangui restores the Western Qin.
410: Southern Yan falls to Liu Yu.
412: Later Qin's Hexi holdings pass out of its hands.
414: the Ordos is gone to Xia.
416: Luoyang falls to Liu Yu.
417: Jin forces enter Chang'an and Yao Hong surrenders.
417: the Later Qin ends.

wars.name: Later Qin-Former Qin war
wars.outcome: Stalemate until "the crucial victory at the Battle of Dajie in 389"; Fu Deng's forces destroyed at Feiqiao in 394; Fu Chong killed by Western Qin forces.

wars.name: Later Qin conquest of Western Qin
wars.outcome: Gangui heavily defeated and surrendered to Southern Liang, later fled to Later Qin; the state revived in 409.

wars.name: Later Qin subjugation of Later Liang
wars.outcome: Guzang besieged 401, Lü Long a vassal, and the whole territory surrendered in 403.

wars.name: Battle of Chaibi
wars.outcome: "a heavy defeat to the Northern Wei at the Battle of Chaibi in 402", halting eastward expansion; no land change on the pages.

wars.name: Restoration of Western Qin
wars.outcome: Gangui restored the Western Qin in 409 and captured several Later Qin commanderies in 410.

wars.name: Liu Yu's conquest of Later Qin
wars.outcome: Luoyang fell in winter 416, Chang'an in spring 417; Yao Hong surrendered; Xia then took the Chang'an region from Liu Yizhen at Qingni (undated).

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the Former Qin remnant, Eastern Jin, Wei and the Hexi states.
